title: A flat ring map of finite presentation is perfect
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts in one line that a ring map which is flat and of finite presentation is perfect (source lines 21814-21817). The proof is a Noetherian-approximation argument. Let A -> B be flat and of finite presentation; it is clear that B has finite tor dimension (proof lines 21820-21821). By the Algebra approximation statement there exists a finite type Z-algebra A_0 contained in A and a flat finite type ring map A_0 -> B_0 such that B = B_0 tensor_{A_0} A (proof lines 21821-21825). By the Noetherian relative pseudo-coherence statement, A_0 -> B_0 is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 21825-21827). Since A_0 -> B_0 is flat, B_0 and A are tor independent over A_0, so the base change statement for relative pseudo-coherence applies and gives that A -> B is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 21828-21831). Together with finite tor dimension this is perfectness. The non-routine content is the reduction to the Noetherian case: every flat finitely presented map is a base change of a flat finite type map of finite type Z-algebras, and pseudo-coherence descends along tor independent base change.
